commits.subject: Withdrawing my own claim from an hour ago: "de L." proves nothing
commits.body:
An hour ago I published that the 1895 census showed a Lerena woman married to a
Lerena man, and called it "the exact pattern the whole search turns on". Then I
went looking for the marriage act I had just said would settle it, and found
something that deflates the claim.
*** THERE IS A JOSEFA LERENA WHO MARRIED FERNANDO MORATORIO. *** Uruguayan
civil registration carries her as the mother of Josefa, Eduardo and Maria
MORATORIO LERENA. FamilySearch's tree attaches that woman to profile
K4VN-52H - "Josefa Lerena Traibel, 1851-1947" - the same candidate.
If that is her, she was "de Moratorio", and "de L." on the census line is the
enumerator's shorthand for THIS HOUSEHOLD - the Lerena house - written against
every married woman in it.
WHAT I READ RIGHT AND WHAT I DID NOT. Re-examined at DeepZoom level 13: line 4
does read "Lerena de L. Josefa", and the "de L." is formed identically to the
two lines above. The LETTER was read correctly. *** The INFERENCE was too
confident. *** Lines 2 and 3 are genuinely "de Lerena" - Justiniana, widow of
Luis Lerena, and Julia Salvanach, wife of Gilberto - so both readings fit them
equally, and neither of them tests the shorthand at all. I had no control case
and did not look for one before publishing.
THE TIERING, PLAINLY. The Moratorio marriage records are INDEX-LEVEL civil
registration - real records. The link from that Josefa to Josefa Lerena Traibel
is a TREE ATTACHMENT, which is SECONDARY and exactly the kind of claim this
archive refuses to build on. So neither side of this is settled: what is settled
is that my census reading is not evidence.
The claim never reached a narrative page - it lived in the register, a data file
and a commit message, and the changelog carries that commit as history. The
correction is on /corrections/ and the register row is retitled from "Josefa
LERENA de Lerena" to "Josefa in Gilberto's 1895 household".
Her marriage act still settles it, and still has not been found. The errand now
says Moratorio or Lerena rather than assuming the answer.

commits.subject: Avelino placed at last, and three Josefas kept apart on purpose
commits.body:
Following the Josefa of the 1895 schedule, and the Lerena Traibel branch this
archive has named since its first week finally attaches.
*** JOSEFA LORENA LERENA TRAIBEL, died Montevideo 2 April 1947, aged NINETY-SIX,
born 1851. "Parents: AMBROCIA TRAIBEL, AVELINO LERENA." ***
So AVELINO LERENA is placed - the head of a branch this archive has referred to
for a fortnight without ever naming him in a record. He is the same forename as
the Avelino Lerena who stood godfather at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1833 to
a child of Justa Pastora Lerena, Sancho's daughter. *** That is suggestive and
no more: no record found here names Avelino's own parents, so he is NOT shown to
be Sancho's son, and the branch is not yet joined to the trunk. ***
*** AND THREE JOSEFAS ARE RECORDED AS THREE ROWS, NOT ONE. *** A Josefa Lerena
stood godmother at Montevideo in 1885; a "Lerena de L. Josefa, 43, viuda" was in
Gilberto's Buenos Aires household in 1895; and this Josefa Lerena Traibel was
born in 1851 and died in 1947. The ages agree within a year and the
identification is strong.
They are deliberately not merged. This archive conflated two Arturo Lerenas
earlier in the same week and had to retract a whole branch within the hour; the
discipline that came out of that is what is being applied. data/josefa-lerena-
candidates.tsv sets out what fits, what does not, and what would settle it - her
MARRIAGE record. If she married a Lerena, the census reading "Lerena de Lerena"
is right, and this family contains a Lerena-Lerena marriage one generation
before Juan Carlos and Maria.
AND A LESSON THAT CUTS AGAINST THE LAST TWO DAYS' ENTHUSIASM. Full-text search
for the compound "Lerena Traibel" returns ZERO. The ordinary name index returns
the branch immediately. *** Full text is not a superset of the name index, and a
null in one is not a null in the other. *** Both sweeps are needed, and the
compound-surname file now says so.
Register: 226 -> 229 people.

commits.subject: The 1895 schedule, read as a household at last - and a Lerena who married a Lerena
commits.body:
This archive has cited the 1895 Buenos Aires census since its first week, for
one name at a time. *** The schedule had never been read as a household. ***
Sixteen people on one page, and it settles three things and opens the sharpest
question in the project.
SETTLED. Don Luis Lerena was DEAD BY 1895: Justiniana is entered "Lenguas de L.
Justiniana, m, 73, VIUDA". His death window closes to 1850-1895, and she was in
Argentina thirteen years earlier than the 1908 evidence.
SETTLED. Gilberto had a TRADE: "CORREDOR DE COMERCIO", a commercial broker,
aged 41. This archive has had him as a breeder and co-founder of the Argentine
Stud Book, which is what he is remembered for. In his own house he told the
enumerator he was a broker.
SETTLED, AND IT IS A CORRECTION TO THIS ARCHIVE. The register carried "Maria
E. C. Lerena, b.1869, daughter of Gilberto (1854)" - which would have made him
FIFTEEN, and which a new consistency check flagged yesterday as impossible. The
schedule shows her SOLTERA at 26, in a house that also holds a JOSEFA, widow of
43. She is not his daughter. "Daughter" was this archive reading a household,
and the household now says otherwise.
*** AND WHAT IT OPENS. *** Line 4 reads "LERENA de L[erena], JOSEFA, m, 43,
VIUDA, R. Oriental". On the two lines above her the same enumerator writes
married women as [maiden surname] + "de L." - Lenguas de Lerena, Salvanach de
Lerena. If he is consistent, *** JOSEFA WAS BORN A LERENA AND MARRIED A
LERENA. ***
That is the exact pattern the whole search turns on. Pablo Armando's enrolment
card names his parents JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA, and the standing
question is whether Maria was a Lerena by birth - a marriage between kin, which
would have needed a dispensation. A Lerena-Lerena marriage in this very family,
one generation earlier, would show the pattern exists.
*** Stated as a reading of an abbreviation in an enumerator's hand, not as a
fact. *** Josefa's own marriage record would settle it and has not been looked
for - logged as an errand, with the note that the dispensation sweep which
concluded no Lerena-Lerena marriage exists is itself now known to be blind to
compound surnames.
She is also, almost certainly, the JOSEFA LERENA who stood godmother to
Gilberto's son Raul at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1885 - a woman this archive
met and could not place.

commits.subject: The living-people rule now gates this build
commits.body:
David's rule across the estate: a LIVING PERSON IS NAMED AND NOTHING MORE —
no date of birth, no date of death, no place. And his age rule: anyone more
than eighty years old is treated as deceased, because an archive that cannot
say whether somebody is alive has to presume something and that is what it
presumes.
Until now Falco was the only archive with a guard, and it had one because the
same date leaked three times — twice from code that read correctly in the
source. Every one was caught by reading the BUILT HTML. Its design is now in
the kit and runs here.
It takes the full date strings the DATA attaches to a living person and
asserts those literal strings appear nowhere in the build. Falco's two earlier
designs are not repeated: bare years pass vacuously on a genealogy site, and
name-near-date fires on every homonym. Identity lives in the data, not the
markup.
An archive that omits living people altogether passes with nothing to check,
which is correct rather than a gap — that rule is stricter than this one.
Verified by planting a guarded date in a build and watching it fail.

commits.subject: The cemetery roll confirms the death a third time
commits.body:
Continuing the compound-surname sweep. "Lerena Lenguas" returns seven
documents, five of them already known - and one that is new and settles
something.
*** DIRECCION DE CEMENTERIOS, MONTEVIDEO - "Relacion de los individuos que han
fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901". *** A civil mortality return, day by
day. Against day 24:
  "24 ... LUIS LERENA LENGUAS"
Between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez.
So the death of 24 December 1901 now rests on THREE independent documents: the
civil death act No. 216, the cemetery office's own roll, and his widow's sworn
statement seven years later when she registered their son's birth. And it
settles in the plainest way that he was BURIED AT MONTEVIDEO.
That matters more than it sounds. Two days ago this archive had published, in
good faith, that he was not in the indexed Uruguayan death registers at all -
a null produced by searching a surname that was filed under SERENA.
*** AND IT WAS FOUND ONLY BY THE COMPOUND SURNAME. *** A search on LERENA does
not reach a table of names like this one: the entry is four words in a column,
with no parish formula around it to match on.

commits.subject: A ninth dispensation, missed by this archive's own sweep of that register
commits.body:
The compound-surname technique found its third and sharpest result, and it is
a correction to work published here on 13 September.
*** EMA SIXTA'S MARRIAGE DISPENSATION EXISTS, AND THE SWEEP MISSED IT. ***
Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, June 1913:
  "Senor Provisor, JOSE PEDRO MASSERA ... digo: que debiendo contraer
   matrimonio con Dona EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO, FELIGRESA DE LA METROPOLITANA
   ... ocurro a V.S. suplicando quiera dispensarme UNA CONCILIAR PROCLAMA ...
   Montevideo, Junio 19 de 1913"
Eleven days before her wedding to the philosopher Massera.
*** AND THE REASON IT WAS MISSED IS STRUCTURAL, NOT BAD LUCK. *** This archive
swept that register on the formula "LERENA FELIGRESA", which assumes the parish
follows the surname immediately. She is written "Lerena JUANICO, feligresa".
The compound surname sits between the two words and the phrase cannot match.
EVERY CHILD OF BOTH MONTEVIDEO COUPLES CARRIES A COMPOUND SURNAME - Lerena
Juanico, Lerena Lenguas, Lerena Salvanach. The sweep was blind to exactly the
people this archive cares most about.
The dispensation file's headline conclusion - no Lerena-Lerena dispensation in
seventy-six years, every Lerena marrying out - is NOT withdrawn. But it rests on
a search now known to be blind, and it is marked as needing a re-run rather than
left standing as though nothing had happened.
THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN TWO DAYS THE SURNAME HAS HIDDEN A RECORD, and
/searched/ now carries all three together: a death filed under SERENA that a
1,502-row sweep walked past; a military rank read as a forename, making a
"Geraldo Dios Lenguas" who never existed; and now a phrase search that cannot
see a woman because her surname is two words long.
The rule is written down: search the COMPOUND surname, the MOTHER'S name, and
the rarest stable word in the household. The bare surname is the search of last
resort, not first.
Also swept and recorded: "Lerena Traibel" returns ZERO, so that branch does not
attach here; Avelino Lerena is real and in the right city in 1836 - godfather to
a foundling named ABELINA for him - but no record names his parents, so he is
still not shown to be Sancho's son.
And the last consistency warning is cleared: Ema Sixta's row now carries an ark.

commits.subject: The sixth child was a Juez de Paz, found by searching the compound surname
commits.body:
Items 13-15, and the last of them turned into the best find of the round.
*** JOSE JULIO LERENA JUANICO WAS A JUDGE. *** Thirty-five Montevideo civil
marriage acts of 1902-1914 open with the formula:
  "Por ante mi JULIO LERENA JUANICO, JUEZ DE PAZ y OFICIAL DEL ESTADO CIVIL de
   la Primera Seccion del Departamento de Montevideo"
One was read in full - Maronas, 28 August 1909. The compound surname is this
family's and no other in the archive; he is the only JULIO among the seven
children; he would be thirty in 1909. Recorded as STRONG BUT NOT PROVED: no act
read so far gives the judge's own parents.
*** AND IT EXPLAINS THE ODDEST THING IN HIS RECORD. *** Jose Julio was born in
March 1879 and his birth was not registered until September 1908, when his
widowed mother of sixty-four swore it before a Juzgado de Paz. This archive
guessed that was proof of birth for a wedding. A man appointed OFICIAL DEL
ESTADO CIVIL needs it rather more than a bridegroom does.
IT WAS FOUND BY SEARCHING THE COMPOUND SURNAME - "Lerena Juanico" - which this
archive had never tried in four days of searching LERENA. That is the same
lesson as the SERENA misindexing and the "Geraldo Dios" ghost, arriving a third
time: the surname is the least reliable handle on this family.
The same search gives a route to the last missing ark, Ema Sixta's marriage of
1913, which should be in those same Montevideo registers.
1882 carried to acts 957-962 - 798 consecutive baptisms read act by act.
What this family now holds on the record: a GENERAL, an ABOGADO, a HACENDADO, a
professor of philosophy by marriage, the co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book,
a PRESIDENT at the font in 1831, an ORIBE for a bride in 1836 - and a JUDGE.
And still no Juan Carlos. Every one of them is documented and none is Pablo
Armando's father.

commits.subject: Her name is Oribe, and this site had it right before I did
commits.body:
Items 8-12 of the fourth fifteen, and a correction that stings.
*** THE FIRST WIFE IS CAROLINA ORIBE, NOT OLIVA. *** I recorded Oliva twice on
14 September - once explicitly to correct an earlier "not confidently legible"
reading - and called it settled. The source of the error was FamilySearch's
index of the 1836 petition, which says Oliva. I read the image expecting Oliva
and saw it.
A Catedral baptism of 4 JULY 1837, in another book and another hand, names
"D. LUIS LERENA y Dna CAROLINA ORIBE" standing godparents to his brother's
child. The petition, re-opened and magnified, reads ORIBE too - a clear b.
*** AND THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN HYPOTHESES PAGE HAD CARRIED, FROM A SECONDARY TREE,
THAT HE MARRIED FIRSTLY A DAUGHTER OF AN ORIBE. *** That line has been on the
site the whole time. I never checked my reading against the page I was editing.
The secondary source was right and the index was wrong.
THE SAME ACT GIVES A SECOND BROTHER: D. PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA, "natural de
esta", same abuelos paternos D. Sancho y Dna Maria Fernandez, married to Vicenta
Vega of Cerro Largo, with a daughter Leonarda Margarita born February 1837. And
it proves Carolina was ALIVE IN JULY 1837 - married September 1836, alive that
July, dead by March 1842.
WHAT ORIBE MEANS, STATED WITH CARE. Manuel Oribe was President of Uruguay
1835-1838 and founder of the Blancos. This family's other documented padrino is
FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, his rival and the founder of the Colorados, who stood at a
Lerena font in 1831. So within five years: Rivera at the font, an Oribe for a
bride - the two men whose quarrel became the Guerra Grande. *** Nothing read
here makes Carolina kin to the president. *** Oribe is a surname, not a proof,
and no record yet names her parents. Recorded as a question, not a descent.
TWO NULLS RE-RUN PROPERLY, since the recordCountry filter was found to break
full-text silently:
- "Juan Carlos Lerena" across the whole corpus returns TWO documents, both
  already known and neither ours. THE CENTRAL NULL HOLDS.
- No child of Luis Lerena and Carolina Oribe. And this null is worth something,
  because the coverage was checked first: the Montevideo registers for 1837-41
  ARE in the corpus - Cordon baptisms 1837-41, Catedral baptisms 1836-40,
  Catedral deaths 1836-42. A machine has read that handwriting and nothing
  returns.
Register: 220 -> 225 people.

commits.subject: Sancho at home in Canelones, 1804 - father, godfather and sworn witness
commits.body:
Items 5-7 of the fourth fifteen. His own marriage act was the target; what came
back was better in one way and does not settle the forename.
*** HIS DAUGHTER, ON A CANELONES ACT OF 15 MAY 1804. ***
  "bautizo en ella solemnemente a una parvula de DOS DIAS nacida, a la cual
   puso por nombre DOMINGA JOSEFA, hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA
   FERNANDEZ; fueron los Padrinos Joseph Ponteceli y Agueda Rivero, TODOS
   VECINOS DE LA MISMA VILLA"
*** SHE IS THE DOMINGA LERENA WHO STOOD GODMOTHER AT THE CATEDRAL IN 1833 ***
to her sister Justa Pastora's child, aged twenty-nine. Yesterday the archive
guessed "almost certainly her sister or cousin". She is the sister - and so
another sister of Don Luis Lerena, now with a birth date.
AND SANCHO IS ATTESTED IN 1804, twenty-seven years earlier than anything held
two days ago. In that one town and that one decade he is a FATHER, a GODFATHER -
standing at the confirmation of "Jose, ESCLAVO DE MANUEL LOPEZ", recorded here
as the act records him, because leaving him out would be a second erasure - and
a SWORN WITNESS in the marriage-investigation files.
Canelones is the family's town, not a line in a published tree: "todos vecinos
de la misma Villa".
*** BUT IT DOES NOT SETTLE SANCHO VERSUS FRANCISCO, and the table now says so
more precisely than I did this morning. *** The count is SIX records saying
Sancho against TWO saying Francisco - and the Francisco pair is NOT simply the
two 1846 transcripts. One of them is the 1833 Catedral act, an original. So
Francisco is not a machine artefact and not only a copyist's slip. A double
forename remains the reading that requires nobody to be wrong, and Sancho's own
marriage act - still unopened - is what would decide it.
A sixth spelling for the file: the machine renders him SANCIO on the 1804
baptism, joining Lerena, Llerena, Lorena, Serena and Lerina.
Register: 217 -> 220 people.

commits.subject: Put the Uruguayan house on the front page, and the President with it
commits.body:
Items 1-4 of the fourth fifteen. All four are the same failure: work done and
not published.
THE RIVERA ACT WAS ON NO PAGE. The first constitutional President of Uruguay
standing godfather to Sancho Llerena's grandson in December 1831 - the most
striking document this archive has found - existed only in a TSV and a register
row. It is now on /hypotheses/ beside the Sancho trunk, and on the front page.
NOR WERE THE TWO EXTRA LENGUAS GENERATIONS. Sixta's death act names Antonio
Lenguas and Juana Grandal, Pascual Gonzalez and Josefa Grandal - the
great-great-grandparents of Luis Eugenio and Gilberto - and the fact that BOTH
GRANDMOTHERS ARE GRANDAL, which makes Pedro and Carmen very probably cousins.
THE FRONT PAGE ENDED BY POINTING THE SEARCH ACROSS THE RIVER and never said
what was found there. It does now - and it keeps the sting in the tail: fifteen
people of the surname are placed in two Montevideo generations, and Juan Carlos
is in none of them.
Also corrected there: the act-by-act read is at 792 baptisms, not the 750 the
panel still claimed.
AND THE DRIFT CHECKER'S FALSE POSITIVES ARE CLEARED. Gilberto's household IS on
/horses/; the matcher was tripping on the word 'assembled', which the page has
no reason to use. Two entries added to PUBLISHED with their reasons. Three real
flags remain and are left standing - the list exists so a genuine one is not
lost in noise, not so I can silence it.

commits.subject: A third of this stylesheet styled another family's pages
commits.body:
Six of the seven archives carry a copy of Defranceschi's stylesheet, and
each uses about half of it. The rest styles pages this archive does not
have and cannot have — Istrian household cards, a Venetian name-form key,
an arms figure, a sovereignty ribbon for the Habsburgs — and it shipped on
every page load.
The read-across is what found it. From inside one repository a rule that
matches nothing looks exactly like a rule for a page you have not written
yet; it is only when Defranceschi comes out at 12 unused classes and
everybody else at 107 to 124 that the shape is obvious.
A rule was removed ONLY when every class in its selector appears nowhere:
not in the built HTML, not in the source, not in the data, not in the kit.
A selector naming one live class was left alone however dead its
companions looked, and element selectors were never touched.
Verified three ways rather than by eye. No class used by any built page
lost its rules — zero, on all seven. The stylesheet still brace-balances.
And on a page of 300 elements, twelve computed properties each, the pruned
sheet and the live one produce byte-identical results.

commits.subject: The "Aguilar" in Sancho's name is supported by nothing this archive has read
commits.body:
A small audit at the end of a large day.
This archive's register calls him "Sancho LLERENA Aguilar". Eight records now
name him, and not one gives him a matronymic. A full-text search for the phrase
"Llerena y Aguilar" returns thirty hits and EVERY ONE IS QUITO, ECUADOR - an
Antonio Llerena y Aguilar who witnesses notarial and probate records there
between 1789 and 1824. A different family on a different continent.
So "Aguilar" comes from the FamilySearch Tree and from nowhere this archive has
read. It is NOT being removed - the tree may rest on an act nobody here has
opened - but it is marked as the unattested part of the name rather than
carried as though documented.
Which leaves this man's identity in a precise and slightly uncomfortable state:
his FORENAME is contested between Sancho and Francisco across eight records;
his MATRONYMIC is unsupported; and the only part every record agrees on is his
wife, MARIA FERNANDEZ.
That is the honest position on the apex of this tree, and it is better than the
one held this morning, when the whole descent was a user-submitted tree entry
with two acts appearing to contradict it.

commits.subject: An original act says Francisco, and my tidy argument does not survive it
commits.body:
I closed the Sancho question this afternoon and reopened it within the hour.
Both the page and the register now say so.
WHAT I ARGUED: that Luis Lerena's father is SANCHO on three original acts -
1836, 1842, 1850 - against only two 1846 entries reading FRANCISCO, and that
those two disqualify themselves because each ends "asi consta del Legajo
conservado en este Archivo": they are later TRANSCRIPTS. Three originals
against two copies is not a conflict.
*** THEN AN ORIGINAL TURNED UP SAYING FRANCISCO. *** Following the new sister
Justa Pastora Lerena to her second child - Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion,
October 1833 - the act names her parents "Maternos: FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria
Fernandez". It is not a copy, and the copies-versus-originals argument dies
with it.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY CONSTANT IS THE WIFE. Maria Fernandez is in every one of these
records without exception, across seventy years and both spellings. Whoever the
man was, he was married to her, and all these people are her descendants.
AND THE READINGS SPLIT ACROSS METHODS, NOT ALONG THEM. The machine transcript
read Sancho in 1831 and Francisco in 1833; I read Francisco off the 1846 images
and Sancho off 1836, 1842 and 1850. So it is not that the machine is unreliable
and I am not, which would have been the comfortable conclusion.
The leading reading is now a DOUBLE FORENAME - Sancho Francisco, or Francisco
Sancho - with clerks using either. Ordinary for the period, and it would mean
nobody is wrong. Two men of one surname each married to a Maria Fernandez is
possible and much less likely. Sancho's own marriage act would settle it and has
never been opened.
The whole table of eight records, with how each was read and whether it is an
original, is in data/sancho-or-francisco.tsv - written at length precisely
because the temptation was to keep the tidy version.
TWO MORE LERENAS out of the same 1833 act: ABELINO and DOMINGA LERENA stood as
its godparents, so almost certainly Justa Pastora's brother and sister. AVELINO
is also the forename attached to the Lerena Traibel branch elsewhere in this
archive - worth testing rather than assuming.
Register: 215 -> 217 people.

commits.subject: The President of Uruguay stood godfather to Sancho Llerena's grandson
commits.body:
Full text came back, and the first hour with it produced the most surprising
document in the archive.
*** CORDON, MONTEVIDEO, 13 DECEMBER 1831. *** The baptism of Juan Facundo
Frutuoso, son of Manuel Zeferino Barros of Pernambuco and of JUSTA PASTORA
LERENA, "natural de Canelones":
  "Abuelos ... Maternos SANCHO LLERENA y MARIA FERNANDEZ ... Fueron Padrinos
   Don FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, PRESIDENTE DE LA REPUBLICA, y su esposa Dona
   BERNARDINA FRAGOSO"
Rivera was the first constitutional President of Uruguay, in office 1830-1834.
The act is of December 1831, squarely in his first term, and the child is named
FRUTUOSO for him.
THREE THINGS COME OUT OF IT.
JUSTA PASTORA LERENA is a DAUGHTER OF SANCHO and a SISTER of Don Luis Lerena -
a person this archive had never met, born at Canelones, married to a Brazilian.
SANCHO IS NAMED IN A FIFTH RECORD, and the first that is not about his son. He
also turns up in person and under oath in the Canelones marriage-investigation
files: "presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le
recivio juramento". Two days ago he was a user-built tree entry that two 1846
transcripts appeared to contradict.
AND THE FAMILY'S STANDING IS NOT WHAT THIS ARCHIVE THOUGHT. It has carried the
Lerenas as obscure - "naturales del E. Oriental" in a Rosario act, a thin and
mostly inferred social picture. Padrinos of that rank are not chosen at random.
It fits everything found since: a GENERAL for a grandfather, an ABOGADO for a
father-in-law, a HACENDADO's death, a marriage to the philosopher Massera,
another to a Magarinos. The pattern is consistent and it starts earlier than
anything here.
Stated carefully: nothing in this act touches Pablo Armando or Juan Carlos. It
is the generation of Sancho's children, sixty years before, and it is recorded
as social context and a new sibling - not as descent.
*** AND A FILTER THAT BREAKS FULL TEXT, recorded so two days are not lost to it
again. *** q.text="Carolina Oliva"&f.recordCountry=Uruguay returns "Something
Went Wrong"; the same query WITHOUT the country filter returns 1,987 results.
Some of what was written up as a two-day outage may simply have been that
filter. Also learned: multiple quoted phrases do NOT AND together, and opening
a result with ?view=fullText puts the machine transcription of the whole
document into the page - which is how the 1831 act was found and read in one
step, without touching a tile.
Register: 209 -> 215 people.

commits.subject: Tell the pages that Sancho stopped being secondary
commits.body:
The drift check flagged it: everything found in the last two days was in the
data and on no page. Caught by the tool rather than by me, which is what it was
written for.
/HYPOTHESES/ STILL TIERED SANCHO AS SECONDARY - "FamilySearch Tree is
user-submitted, and nobody here has opened the fourteen acts". Three acts
naming him as Luis Lerena's father have now been opened, and the page says so:
  1836 - Luis Lerena's own marriage petition, over his own signature
  1842 - his second marriage, to Justiniana Lenguas
  1850 - the baptism of his son Alberto Octavio
And the two 1846 entries that read FRANCISCO, and briefly looked like they
would topple the whole descent, disqualify themselves in their own last line:
they are later transcripts copied out of a legajo. Three originals against two
copies is not a conflict.
The page is careful about WHAT changed. The 1767 birth at Cordoba, the 1791
marriage at Canelones, the fourteen attached acts - all still secondary and
still unopened. What moved is the JOIN: Sancho to Luis, and so to everyone
below him. That is the part the whole tree hangs from.
It also now carries the marriage nobody knew about: Luis Lerena married DONA
CAROLINA OLIVA of Montevideo in September 1836 and was her widower by March
1842. Any children of that marriage are half-siblings of Luis Eugenio and
Gilberto. The indexed records hold no trace - stated as a null, not an answer,
because the Montevideo registers of 1837-41 are largely un-indexed.
/HORSES/ NOW CARRIES HIS HOUSEHOLD, in the two halves it falls into: four
children christened at Montevideo to 31 October 1886, four at Buenos Aires from
29 October 1890. *** So the crossing is bracketed by baptisms rather than
inferred from census birthplaces *** - records of the family, not of what its
children later said about themselves. And Juan Carlos is not among the eight,
which matters because this was the best remaining place to put him.

commits.subject: The 1836 marriage left no trace but its own petition
commits.body:
Following the first wife forward, and reporting the null rather than a hope.
Two searches for children of Luis Lerena and Carolina Oliva:
  - Any record pairing a LERENA father with a CAROLINA OLIVA mother, worldwide:
    ONE result, a 1928 marriage in Minas Gerais to a Joaquim Alves de Lorena.
    Not ours.
  - Any Carolina Oliva in Uruguay 1830-1850: 1,507 rows, and every one of them
    is a LATER woman - the Carolina Oliva who married Antonio Reverditto and
    bore children from 1879. No death for ours, and no child.
So the marriage of September 1836 left nothing in the indexed records but the
petition itself. Six years, a wife who died, and not one indexed baptism or
burial.
*** RECORDED AS A NULL AND NOT AS AN EXCLUSION. *** The Montevideo registers of
1837-1841 are largely un-indexed, and this archive has learned twice this week
exactly what indexes miss: a death filed under SERENA that eight sweeps walked
past, and a general's rank turned into the forename "Geraldo Dios". Finding
nothing in an index is not finding nothing.
What it would actually take is written down instead: the Montevideo baptism
registers for 1837-1841 turned by hand, and the burials for 1841-42. That is
the same size of job as the Rosario reads already under way, and it is stated
at its real size rather than left as a hopeful line.

commits.subject: The first wife has a name: Carolina Oliva, Montevideo, 3 September 1836
commits.body:
An hour after learning that Don Luis Lerena had been married before, the
marriage itself was found - and it closes a question this archive opened
yesterday morning.
*** THE PETITION OF 3 SEPTEMBER 1836. *** On the stamped paper of that year,
in Luis Lerena's own hand and over his own signature - the only signature of
this man anywhere in the archive:
  "D. LUIS LERENA, natural de esta Ciudad, hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO LERENA
   y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ ... tiene concertado matrimonio con Dona
   CAROLINA OLIVA, tambien natural de esta Ciudad"
He asks to be excused the usual enquiry "en atencion a ser ambos nativos de
esta Ciudad, y bastante conocidos" - a small social fact about the family in
1836, and the first this archive has had.
*** SANCHO IS NOW CLOSED. *** Yesterday morning two 1846 baptism transcripts
named Luis Lerena's father as FRANCISCO, and the Andalusian apex of this whole
tree looked wrong. He is now named in FOUR records - this petition of 1836, the
second marriage of 1842, the baptism of Alberto Octavio in 1850, and that act's
index - and 1836 is the earliest and plainest of them. The two dissenting
entries say of themselves that they are later transcripts copied from a legajo.
A copy and three originals is not a conflict.
AND THE SURNAME I COULD NOT READ IS OLIVA. The 1842 act calls him "viudo de
Dona Carolina" and I could not make out the surname, so I wrote down what it
looked like - something like Dille or Dulce - and said plainly it was not
confidently legible. It is OLIVA. The wrong reading is left in the record
rather than deleted, because the next person squinting at that word should know
what it is not. The lesson is the cheaper one: I searched for the marriage
instead of squinting harder.
*** WHAT IS NOW OPEN. *** Between September 1836 and March 1842 there is a
marriage nobody here knew about. If it produced children they are HALF-SIBLINGS
of Luis Eugenio and Gilberto - Lerenas of the right surname, born at Montevideo
in the late 1830s - and they are a place Juan Carlos has never been looked for.
Logged with exactly what to search: Montevideo baptisms 1837-1841 to Luis
Lerena and Carolina Oliva, and Carolina's death.

commits.subject: Luis Lerena married twice, and Sancho is named in a third act
commits.body:
Found by searching the surname LENGUAS in ARGENTINA - which nobody had thought
to do, because this has been treated throughout as a Uruguayan family.
*** THE MARRIAGE OF LUIS LERENA AND JUSTINIANA LENGUAS, 3 MARCH 1842. *** The
generation above the Montevideo trunk, marrying. Eleven months before Luis
Eugenio was born on 9 February 1843; the fit is exact.
  "desposé en SEGUNDAS NUPCIAS a D. LUIS LERENA, natural de la Ciudad de
   Montevideo, de treinta anos de edad, hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO y Dona
   MARIA FERNANDEZ, VIUDO de Dona CAROLINA ...; [con] JUSTINIANA LENGUAS ...
   de veinte anos, hija legitima del Sr. GRAL. Lenguas y Dona Carmen Gonzalez"
*** HE WAS A WIDOWER, AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NO IDEA. *** Luis Lerena married
before about 1841 a Carolina who was dead by March 1842. If that marriage
produced children, there is an ENTIRE HALF-SIBLING GENERATION to Luis Eugenio
and Gilberto - Lerenas of the right surname, the right country and the right
generation - that nothing here has ever looked for. Logged as an errand.
SANCHO FOR THE THIRD TIME, and this is the earliest of the three. The 1850
baptism said Sancho; this says Sancho in 1842. Against them stand two 1846
entries reading "Francisco", and those two say of themselves that they are
later TRANSCRIPTS copied from a legajo. The apex of this tree is now as well
attested as anything in it - and it was in doubt yesterday morning.
THE GENERAL CONFIRMED IN A SECOND ACT, four years earlier than the baptism that
first gave him the rank. And it explains a FamilySearch ghost: the index of this
act renders "Gral. D. Pedro" as a forename - "Geraldo Dios Lenguas" - which is
how a military rank becomes a christian name and a searchable person who never
existed.
Also: Luis Lerena born about 1812 and stated MONTEVIDEAN; Justiniana about 1822,
agreeing exactly with her stated 79 in 1901 and 87 in 1908.
ONE THING LEFT OPEN RATHER THAN GUESSED. FamilySearch files this under Buenos
Aires, San Miguel Arcangel - but the officiant describes himself as "Cura Rector
de la Parroquia de Nuestra Senora del Carmen del SALTO ORIENTAL DEL URUGUAY".
The act is in an Argentine book; where the ceremony happened is not settled by
what is legible, and is recorded as unsettled.
And a new parish to search: the 1914 informacion says Carlos Lerena was
"bautizado en la Iglesia de el CORDON, Dep. de Montevideo" - a third Montevideo
parish for this family, never searched.
Register: 207 -> 208 people.

commits.subject: Gilberto's Argentine household, and the crossing bracketed by baptisms
commits.body:
Continuing. The confirmations advanced, the sharpest lead was finally run, and
a claim I made this morning was wrong.
*** I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CONFIRMATIONS THIS MORNING. *** From the first
eleven entries I recorded that "EVERY ENTRY ON THIS PAGE IS A GIRL" and built a
search strategy on it - that a boy of eight would be in a separate run of pages,
and that is where to look. Entries 133, 135 and 138 on a later page are Domingo,
Santiago and Pablo, all "hijo leg. de", mixed straight in among the girls. I
made a structure out of eleven rows. There is no boys' section and no shortcut.
Read since: entries 45-88, 133-177 and 222-243 of the 26 March 1890 sitting -
which runs past 243 children - and the opening of a SECOND 1890 sitting in June
and July. No Lerena. Ages run from two to fourteen in one sitting, so nobody is
ruled in or out by age. And a false alarm checked and dismissed: two words in
the June list are struck through and read like a surname at low resolution;
at full resolution they are "Silvero" and "Laurino", the clerk correcting a
forename.
GILBERTO'S ARGENTINE HOUSEHOLD, assembled for the first time - the job that was
blocked yesterday when their search went down. Searching him AS FATHER gives
EIGHT children by Julia Salvanach: Gilberto (1878), Carlos (1884), Raul Alfredo
Luis (1885) and Maria Angelica Julia (1886), all born at MONTEVIDEO; then Maria
Carlota (1890), Luis Felipe (1892), Cesar Alberto (1896) and Horacio Alfredo
(1898), at BUENOS AIRES.
*** SO THE CROSSING IS NOW BRACKETED BY BAPTISMS RATHER THAN INFERRED. *** The
last Montevideo baptism is 31 October 1886; the first Buenos Aires one is 29
October 1890. This archive has said "between 1887 and 1889", read off the switch
in census birthplaces. The baptisms are slightly wider and considerably firmer:
they are records of the family, not of its children's stated origins.
And Juan Carlos is not among them. That matters, because this was the best
remaining place to put him - a Lerena household of the right surname, in the
right country, at the right time, descending from the one Uruguayan house this
archive has documented.
THE ALEJANDRO TEST WAS RUN AND CAME BACK INCONCLUSIVE, which is recorded as
inconclusive. Alejandro Lerena Lenguas was born 29 May 1845; the enrolment
cards name an ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA born Uruguay 1839, married Julia Bassani,
with a large Buenos Aires family. Six years apart, well inside the range this
archive keeps meeting between an act and a stated age - but nothing positive
links them and NO RECORD FOUND NAMES ALEJANDRO MAXIMO'S PARENTS.
The search did establish there are at least THREE distinct men of the name,
including one of the Trinidad orbit married to Severa Fernandez. They are kept
as three rows deliberately; merging them is the easy mistake here.
Register: 202 -> 207 people.

commits.subject: Canonical URLs keep their trailing slash
commits.body:
These sites build with format: 'directory', so /TheX is a redirect to /TheX/.
The home page's canonical was pointing at the redirect.

commits.subject: This archive now has a face when somebody shares it
commits.body:
Paste this archive into a message and it showed the bare address: no title,
no description, no icon, nothing. Blazevic and the children's site have done
it properly all along — the implementation existed, in this estate, working,
and six archives never received it. The read-across is what surfaced it,
because a missing tag is invisible from inside one repository.
The head tags now come from the kit's SocialHead, which derives everything
from archives.json through BASE_URL rather than taking it as typed values. A
looked-up accent cannot end up being another archive's: Blazevic had been
shipping theme-color #1F5C6B, the teal it gave up in Phase 1.
The favicon is this archive's own accent, so the seven are told apart in a
tab strip the same way they are told apart on the page.
Nothing claims an asset that is not on disk — an archive with no share image
emits a summary card rather than a link to a picture that was never made.

commits.subject: Open the confirmations at last, and learn to tell an outage from a block
commits.body:
Items 9-15 of the third fifteen. Three registers advanced, three jobs blocked,
and the blockage itself turned into the most reusable thing here.
THE CONFIRMATIONS ARE OPEN. Listed as untried since this archive's first week,
without a film number until yesterday, and serving no tiles when first tried -
which turned out to be part of an outage, not a restriction. DGS 4531018, 421
images, unrestricted, and it works today.
It is a better register than expected. The confirmations of 26 March 1890 at
Rosario are a numbered list, and *** every entry names the child's PARENTS ***.
Pablo Armando was born in February 1882; the children confirmed that day are
aged six to fifteen. He is squarely in range, and his parents are the question.
Two things from the first page: no Lerena in eleven entries - and EVERY ONE OF
THEM IS A GIRL. If the confirmations were taken sex by sex, a boy of eight is
in a separate run of pages, and that is where to look. Also: the entries carry
only a GIVEN name, so the surname has to be read out of the father's - this
register cannot be scanned down a margin the way the baptisms were.
DEATH REGISTERS, two more openings, 22 July to 14 August 1841. No Lerena. And
two facts that change the estimate for anyone attempting the whole thing: the
film carries a *** "POOR COPY - WHOLE VOLUME" *** target card, which is
FamilySearch's own warning on the filming of the entire volume, and the film
contains RE-SHOTS - image i=6 is i=5 again behind that card - so 658 images is
not 658 openings.
1882: acts 951-956. 792 consecutive baptisms now read act by act.
AND THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Three jobs stalled on FamilySearch, and the failures
were not all the same failure. Recorded as its own file:
  catalogue SEARCH      - "Something Went Wrong". Their outage.
  catalogue BY ID       - WORKED THROUGHOUT, while its own search box was dead.
                          Every DGS number recovered in two days came out of it.
  full-text search      - down both days. The dispensations live there, which
                          is why that job is still blocked.
  records search        - worked most of two days, then began returning AN
                          EMPTY BODY - zero bytes, no error page - for a query
                          that had worked twenty minutes before.
  image tiles           - SERVED NORMALLY THROUGHOUT, both days, while every
                          search surface was failing.
The empty body is the quiet one. A real null returns a page saying so; anything
that reports "0 results" off a zero-length body is reporting the outage and not
the records. That is a way to publish a false negative without noticing, and
this archive has published enough true negatives to care about the difference.
Reading stopped when that third mode appeared rather than being pushed through.
FamilySearch has firewalled this session before, caused by reading rate. A block
costs days; waiting costs hours.
The three blocked jobs are logged with what to do: trace Gilberto's Buenos
Aires household forward (the sharpest lead in the archive now he is attached -
his son married there in 1914 and his mother was living in Argentina at 87);
test whether Alejandro Lerena Lenguas, b.1845, is the Alejandro M. Lerena of
the enrolment cards; and find General Pedro Lenguas, whose own parents are now
known, in Uruguayan military history rather than in FamilySearch.

commits.subject: A second witness from another parish, and the Lenguas back two more generations
commits.body:
Items 5-8 of the third fifteen. Three images opened; each corrected or extended
something this archive already held.
THE SECOND WITNESS TO GILBERTO'S PARENTAGE. Act 1447 was read yesterday and
made him a brother of Luis Eugenio. The second image - never opened - is the
baptism of his son RAUL ALFREDO LUIS at the CATEDRAL BASILICA de Montevideo,
10 September 1885, folio 296: "hijo legitimo de Gilberto Lerena y Julia
Salvanach, orientales: abuelos paternos LUIS y JUSTINIANA LENGUAS: abuelos
maternos CRISTOBAL y ANGELA ALVAREZ."
Identical to act 1447 - but a different year, a different parish and a
different priest's hand. Two independent registers agreeing is a different kind
of evidence from one register read twice. It also identifies the "Raul Lerena,
b.1885 Montevideo" of the 1895 Buenos Aires census, and turns up a JOSEFA
LERENA at the font whom this archive has never met.
THE RETIRO RECORD CORRECTED THIS ARCHIVE TWICE. The register called it a
"Retiro BAPTISM"; it is an INFORMACION MATRIMONIAL, which is why it names both
parties' parents and baptismal parishes. And the father read as "ALBERTO
(almost certainly GILBERTO)" is written GILBERTO plainly - the archive's own
guess was right and can stop being one. It also says where Carlos was baptised:
the Iglesia del CORDON, Montevideo - a third parish for this family, and an
exact place to look next.
SIXTA'S DEATH ACT PUTS THE SISTERS FINDING ON AN IMAGE - and reaches two
generations further than anything this archive has held. "Hija de D. PEDRO
LENGUAS y de Dona CARMEN GONZALEZ, finados; sus abuelos paternos D. ANTONIO
LENGUAS y Dona JUANA GRANDAL; maternos D. PASCUAL GONZALEZ y Dona JOSEFA
GRANDAL." Her husband: "D. CANDIDO JUANICO, Oriental, edad 72 anos, viudo,
ABOGADO" - born about 1812, and a lawyer, which is what the archive's "Dr." has
always rested on.
BOTH GRANDMOTHERS ARE GRANDAL - Juana and Josefa. Pedro Lenguas and Carmen
Gonzalez were very probably cousins. Recorded as an observation; no record read
here links the two women directly. And an Antonio Lenguas BORN 1807 AT BUENOS
AIRES, buried 1841 at Las Piedras with a wife Juana Grandal, is already in the
indexed records - almost certainly this man, which would make the Lenguas a
Buenos Aires family before a Montevideo one.
THE LAST ARK IS STILL MISSING, and the errand now says exactly why. Ema Sixta's
marriage act is not name-indexed at image level: searching her with Massera as
spouse returns only her children's records, and searching Massera for 1912-14
returns passenger lists. What would work is browsing the La Union film by DGS,
which needs the catalogue opened BY ID rather than by its search box.
And the emphasis guard earned its place again: my own edit orphaned a closing
marker in the Carlos note, and the build refused to ship it.
Register: 197 people -> 201.

commits.subject: Publish act 1447, and stop two pages calling it unopened
commits.body:
Items 1-4 of the third fifteen. All four are corrections to yesterday.
TWO PAGES WERE CARRYING FALSE CLAIMS, and they were false because of my own
work an hour later. /horses/ said the brotherhood was "still not primary -
neither image has been opened". /hypotheses/ said "still index-level: two
entries agree and neither image has been opened". Act 1447 was opened about an
hour after both sentences were written, and both stood for a day.
AND THE ACT ITSELF WAS ON NO PAGE AT ALL. The best document this archive has
found - four grandparents in one line, and Luis Eugenio's own wife at the font
for his brother's child - existed only in the register and a TSV. The word
"godmother" appeared nowhere on the site. It is now quoted in full on /horses/,
where the seven mentions of Gilberto live.
Both pages now say what happened rather than what was true for an hour: the
superseded sentences are named, not silently deleted, because a page that
quietly edits its own history is worth less than one that shows its working.
TWO ERRANDS LIED AGAIN. "Open the images behind Gilberto's parentage" was still
marked ready - it was done, and it came out primary. Its detail now carries the
act, the ark and the fact that THE SECOND IMAGE IS STILL UNOPENED, which is the
part that matters for whoever picks it up.
AND THE DRIFT CHECK CAUGHT THE OTHER ONE ITSELF - an errand marked ready whose
own detail said DONE. But it then fired twice more on rewording, because it was
matching "DONE" and "FOUND" ANYWHERE in the detail, and hit "a trap FOUND on the
way" and "four of the five are DONE" - progress narration inside a legitimately
open errand. It now only reads the first ninety characters, where a claim that
the whole errand is finished would actually be made. A check that fires on
honest narration teaches people to ignore it.

commits.subject: Repin the kit, or every deploy breaks on the new check
commits.body:
The build now runs checkarchive.py out of node_modules, and CI installs the
kit with `npm ci` — which honours the lockfile, not the branch. The lockfile
still pointed at b5b7459, a kit commit from before that file existed, so CI
would have installed a kit without it and failed on the very first build.
Repinned to d4a53e0 and verified the way CI does it: node_modules wiped,
npm ci, build. The check runs and passes.

commits.subject: The shared end-to-end test now gates this build
commits.body:
All seven archives now run one test, from the kit, against the built site:
links, anchors, contents lists, the search index, the sibling ring, the
confidence vocabulary, the visit counter, titles, images and the sitemap.
This archive passes it clean, so it is wired into `build` — a broken internal
link or a search index pointing at pages that were never built can no longer
reach the deploy.
The four archives that do not pass yet have the script but not the gate.
Gating a failing build is not a fix, it is an outage.

commits.subject: Start the death registers, carry 1882 on, and recover five film numbers
commits.body:
Items 11-14 of the second fifteen. Two done, one started, one blocked by an
outage - and the outage taught something worth keeping.
ITEM 11, THE DEATH REGISTERS, STARTED. DGS 4531021, "Defunciones 1841-1860",
658 images, unrestricted - and the leader card reads film 1091422, matching the
catalogue exactly, so the mapping is verified rather than assumed. First opening
read: five acts, 26 May to 18 June 1841 - Juan Fernandez, Luisa Candelaria
Bravo, Victoria Medina, Ynnocencia Villa Real, Maria Zumbero. No Lerena. Many
are "parbula" and "limosna": infants, buried on charity.
The margin-name method works here exactly as on the baptisms, and the structure
is now known: five or six acts a page, chronological, names in the margin. That
puts 1841-1860 alone on the order of six thousand acts. STARTED, NOT FINISHED,
and the file says so with an exact resume point.
Worth being clear about what this read is FOR. It cannot find Pablo Armando -
he was born in 1882, four decades later. It can find whether any LERENA died at
Rosario between 1841 and 1860, which would mean a Lerena was living there long
before him. This archive's whole argument is that they were not a Rosario
family. So this read exists to try to prove the archive wrong, and that is the
reason to do it.
ITEM 12: acts 945-950, 9-10 August 1882 - Toledo, Dolmas, Perez, Candelaria,
Orellana, Ferrari. No Lerena. 786 consecutive baptisms now read act by act.
ITEM 14: FIVE FILM NUMBERS RECOVERED that this archive had listed without them,
including *** Confirmaciones 1883-1918, DGS 4531018, 421 images, unrestricted -
the one that covers Pablo Armando. *** He was born in February 1882 and would
have been confirmed in the 1890s, and a confirmation act commonly names the
parents. The confirmations have been listed as untried since the first week and
never had a film number. Also Confirmaciones 1722-1833/1860-1895 and 1764-1833,
and Matrimonios 1722-1803 and 1804-1852.
The film itself opened but served no tiles and put no ark in the page title,
unlike every other film handled today, so it is logged as needing another
attempt rather than another search.
ITEM 13 IS STILL BLOCKED, and by their outage rather than by the work. The
dispensations live in the FULL-TEXT corpus, not a name-indexed collection, and
full-text search was down all session.
AND THE DIAGNOSTIC, which is the useful part: catalogue SEARCH, full-text
search and /search/film/<old film number> were all returning "Something Went
Wrong" for hours - while name-indexed records search and, crucially, DIRECT
CATALOGUE IDs worked perfectly. Every one of those five DGS numbers came out of
https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog/208788 while the catalogue's own
search box was dead. So when the catalogue looks dead, open the ID directly
before concluding the work cannot be done. Written into the film table.

commits.subject: Justiniana and Sixta were sisters, and Sancho is now on an act
commits.body:
Item 15 of the second fifteen - the one real question on the list - answered,
and it answered more than it was asked.
THE QUESTION: Candido Juanico's second wife was a LENGUAS, and his daughter by
his first wife married a Lerena LENGUAS. Were the two women kin? If so, these
families were joined before the 1864 marriage this archive has treated as the
join.
THE ANSWER IS YES, AND FROM TWO DIRECTIONS. Sixta Lenguas's death registration
of 17 January 1884 names her parents as "Pedro Lenguas, Carmen Gonzalez" and
her husband as "Candido Juanico". The 1846 baptisms of Luis Eugenio and his
sister name Justiniana's parents as the same couple - one of them calling him
"el GENERAL D. Pedro Lenguas", a rank no other record here gives.
*** SO WHEN LUIS EUGENIO MARRIED JULIA JUANICO IN DECEMBER 1864, THE GROOM'S
MATERNAL AUNT WAS ALREADY THE BRIDE'S STEPMOTHER. *** The families had been
joined since 1857. The wedding this archive has read as the join was the second
knot, not the first.
AND THE APEX ANCESTOR GOT A FRIGHT, THEN A PROMOTION. The 1846 acts name Luis
Lerena's father as FRANCISCO - not SANCHO, the Andalusian soldier this archive
puts at the top of the line. On those two acts the whole descent looked wrong.
So the decisive record was opened the same hour rather than left as a doubt:
act 585 of 7 October 1850, S. Agustin, pueblo de la Restauracion.
  "hijo legitimo de D. Luis Lerena y D. Justiniana Lenguas, naturales de
   Montevideo. PATERNOS: D. SANCHO y D. MARIA FERNANDEZ."
Sancho stands - and now stands on an ACT rather than on an index and a
published tree, which this archive had explicitly marked SECONDARY. The 1846
entries lose because of what they say about themselves: each ends "asi consta
del Legajo conservado en este Archivo, mandado trasladar por el Sr. Obispo" -
they are later TRANSCRIPTS, at one remove. A copy and an original disagreeing
is a copy being wrong. The discrepancy is recorded rather than tidied away.
ALSO OUT OF THOSE TWO IMAGES: a sixth sibling, ALEJANDRO LERENA; General Pedro
Lenguas and Carmen Gonzalez as a couple; Maria Fernandez, who is where the "y
Fernandez" in Luis Lerena's name comes from; three more Lenguas at the font;
Luis Eugenio's true birth date, 9 February 1843; and two indexing errors -
"Alberto Otario" is ALBERTO OCTAVIO, and "Justinia" is JUSTINIANA MAURICIA
MAXIMA.
TWO GUARDS ADDED, both of which found something immediately:
- A near-duplicate check. build-people.py refuses EXACT duplicate names, so
  those never happen; it could not see "Dona Sixta LENGUAS (2nd wife...)" and
  "Dona Sixta LENGUAS Gonzalez (2nd wife...)", two rows for one woman written
  hours apart today. Merged. It carries a CHECKED_PAIRS list in the sibling
  convention, where adding a pair is a claim that somebody looked.
- It also flagged MARIA E. C. LERENA, "born 1869, daughter of Gilberto (1854)"
  - which would make him FIFTEEN. All the record says is that she was in his
  household at the 1895 census; "daughter" was this archive's reading of a
  household, not the census's word. Left in place with the contradiction
  stated against it.
Register: 188 people -> 195.

commits.subject: Gilberto is a brother on a document, and his sister-in-law stood godmother
commits.body:
Items 7-10 of the second fifteen. Three images opened; the biggest of them
settles the archive's loudest coincidence.
ACT 1447, SAN FRANCISCO DE ASIS, 31 OCTOBER 1886. Gilberto Lerena's daughter
Maria Angelica Julia, "hija legitima de Don Gilberto Lerena y de Dona Julia
Salvanach, ORIENTALES" - and the paternal grandparents are named: "Don LUIS y
Dona JUSTINIANA LENGUAS". The same couple named as Luis Eugenio's parents in
his marriage act of 1864 and his death act of 1901.
So the co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book and the man whose daughter was the
single Lerena baptised at Rosario in a hundred and seventy years are BROTHERS,
and it is now a priest's hand that says so rather than a tree. This archive had
carried it as secondary since 8 September - Geneanet, Geni, a blog - and as a
strong lead since this morning.
AND THE GODMOTHER IS DONA JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA. Luis Eugenio's own wife
stood at the font for her husband's brother's child. The two households are not
merely related on paper; they are one family acting as one. Written by Martin
Perez, the same priest who wrote act 1720 for Candido Jaime that year.
ACT 283 OF 1908 - JOSE JULIO'S BIRTH, declared by HIS OWN MOTHER. Julia
Juanico, 64, a widow of calle Buenos Aires 102, walked into the Juzgado de Paz
two years before her death and registered the birth of a son born in 1879 at
calle Yi 303. Two things fall out of it:
- It INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS the death found this morning. A different document,
  written seven years later by his widow, gives the identical date: "fallecido
  en esta Ciudad el veinte y cuatro de Diciembre de mil novecientos uno". The
  death act was found under the misspelling SERENA; this one under LERENA.
- *** JUSTINIANA LENGUAS WAS ALIVE AT EIGHTY-SEVEN AND LIVING IN ARGENTINA. ***
  She was 79 and in Montevideo at her son's death in 1901. By 1908 the matriarch
  had crossed the river - and her son GILBERTO had moved to Buenos Aires between
  1887 and 1889.
ACTS 404 AND 405 OF 1843 - JULIA'S OWN BAPTISM, and a name trap. Born 23
November 1842, "hija legitima de D. Candido Juanico y D. Juliana Joaquina
Gonzalez". Act 404 immediately above baptises ENRIQUE JUANICO, born 18 May 1841
- a BROTHER, christened the same day, he at two and a half and she at ten and a
half months. And Julia's own godfather is ALSO a D. Enrique Juanico. A boy of
two cannot stand godfather, so these are two different men and the register
keeps them as two rows deliberately.
THE ARK AUDIT: three of five rows claiming IMAGE READ now carry one, and
Bartolome Llerena was re-opened and checked line by line - "Llerena / Bartolome
/ 45", the double L exactly as read. A trap found on the way, and recorded: the
film's own ?i=86 is NOT the page this archive called image 86. It lands on an
Aguirrebarrena household with no Llerena on it. The ark came from his index
record instead. Two rows still lack arks and say so.
Register: 183 people -> 188.

commits.subject: Tell the pages what the data learned, and write the check that noticed
commits.body:
Items 1-6 of the second fifteen. All six are corrections to my own work.
/HORSES/ DID NOT KNOW. It named Gilberto Lerena seven times as an unplaced
coincidence - "a Lerena at the centre of Argentine breeding, in the right
country at the right time" - and footnoted the brotherhood as PUBLISHED
GENEALOGY, secondary, Geneanet and a blog. That footnote went out of date the
moment two Uruguayan parish records named his parents. It now says so, and says
what came with it: Luis Eugenio's death act, his mother alive at 79, and his
trade - HACENDADO, a landowner, which is a rather different neighbour for a
stud than a name on a blog.
/HYPOTHESES/ SAID IT WAS WAITING for exactly what had happened. Its own words:
"that is the best that can be said until the Montevideo registers are opened".
They were opened the same day. The page now answers its own sentence - and
keeps the two things that did NOT move, which is that none of it finds Juan
Carlos and none of it connects Pablo Armando to that household.
TWO MORE FINDINGS WERE IN THE DATA AND ON NO PAGE:
- The Trinidad wives. BELOQUI and ECHEVERRY are Basque, and PELAEZ is the
  family the Lerenas married so repeatedly they needed dispensing for
  consanguinity by 1885. Published at /name/, and carefully: it is evidence
  about the community they married into, NOT about the etymology, and the
  Basque-or-Extremaduran fork stays open.
- The Serena misindexing, and the rule that came out of it. Published at
  /searched/ with both of the negatives it overturned left standing beside it,
  because a page of failures that deletes its own failures is worth nothing.
THREE ERRANDS WERE LYING. "Find the death of Luis Eugenio" still said ready,
and its detail put the window from 1880 - wrong twice over, since his last child
was born 1884 and the death was found. "Turn the dispensation register" was
marked DONE on the strength of a full-text search, and turning is not searching;
that distinction is the whole reason the task exists. And one errand still told
the reader that FamilySearch had firewalled this session and refused every
request - true when written, false since, and left standing it would stop the
next person from trying.
AND tools/drift.py, in the sibling convention. It compares what the data knows
against what the pages claim. On its first run it found the Basque wives.
*** IT WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THE GILBERTO FAILURE, and the file says so. ***
I tested it against precisely that case by stripping the fix back out of both
pages, and it stayed quiet: the words of the claim were already on /searched/
from the marriage-act writeup. A new relationship between two people the site
already discusses introduces no new vocabulary, and a word-presence check cannot
see it. Written into the docstring so nobody reads a clean run as proof.
Getting there took three wrong versions, each caught by testing rather than
assumed: scoring on word LENGTH let "parents" and "September" dilute the signal;
checking the whole CORPUS could not tell whether any single page made the claim;
and a three-word floor skipped short claims entirely - which is how it first
missed the very finding it was written for. It also cried wolf at 28 findings
until it was narrowed to people the narrative is actually about.
Prints only, never fails the build, and carries a PUBLISHED list in which
adding a name is a claim that somebody looked.

commits.subject: The other Mary Ann Brayley, read at the registry rather than quoted
commits.body:
The WikiTree section on this page rests an exclusion on one thin source: a
Queensland death-registration index entry naming a man's mother. It has now
been read at the Queensland registry itself.
George James Yelland died 29 August 1945, registration 1945/B/3228, mother
entered as Mary Ann Brayley, father as William. The profile was quoting it
accurately.
And the Queensland household turns out to be fully registered and entirely
separate: he married Catherine Pye on 4 February 1892, and Walter, Ernest and
Gertrude Fanny are registered at Brisbane in 1893, 1894 and 1896. A complete
family with its own Mary Ann Brayley behind it. Ours married William Taylor
and died at Northam in Devon on 21 April 1900, and cannot have been doing
both. The exclusion was right; it now rests on the registration instead of on
somebody's summary of it.
The nulls with it: across births to 1926, marriages to 1951 and deaths to
1996, Queensland holds no LERENA and no JUANICO. Every LLERENA, LARENA and
LERINA hit is the word used as a given name — Llerena Lenore Meston, Lerina
Hood, Erinn Larena Petersen — and none is a surname. Worth writing down
because this line does reach Brisbane in the end, by way of South Africa, and
somebody will wonder whether it got there sooner.

commits.subject: The counter goes live
commits.body:
All seven codes are in, each checked against its own endpoint first rather
than assumed: every one answers 200 with the public counter switched on.
The footer now carries the running total, the tracking script that feeds
it, and a line saying who is counting and that it is done without cookies.

commits.subject: Trees: the nav link, and the doors
commits.body:
Two things the last pass dropped. Moving the entry into Start removed
D'Arcy's link and the reinsertion failed silently, so the page existed with
nothing pointing at it. And Lerena's rows were written before the component
gained its closing doors, so it stopped dead where the others send you on.

commits.subject: A public read count in the footer
commits.body:
You asked for the number on the page rather than in a dashboard, which
decided the tool: GoatCounter publishes a count you can display, and
Cloudflare and Plausible keep theirs private.
It is no-cookie and retains no personal data, which matters more than usual
on seven public sites about living relatives. The footer says so, and links
to them, so a reader can see who is counting.
Nothing renders until an archive has a code: no script, no request, no
placeholder. If the counter cannot be reached the line removes itself
rather than showing a nought that is not true.
The codes are empty in the kit's archives.json. Creating the accounts needs
a sign-up, which is not something I can do — the one manual step is in the
covering note.

commits.subject: Trees: bring the page up to the standard, not just the shape
commits.body:
The structure shipped; the content did not. Three faults, all mine.
The nav entry went into whatever menu happened to hold a tree-ish page —
"In Britain" here, "Her life" on Blazevic — where the reference puts it
under Start. It is under Start on all seven now.
The prose was generated filler. Worse, running .capitalize() over each
archive's own blurb lower-cased its proper nouns: "Ivy miriam sneyd's
people, of boulia and brisbane." Every row is now written, with the facts
this archive actually holds, and the archive's own casing is left alone.
Fewer rows and better ones. Eleven thin lines become six that say
something: the spine, the two grafts, and the three families that carry
real weight. The rest are one click away on /families/, which is where
they belong.
The page now opens on the editorial point the reference leads with — a
tree with invented joins in it is worse than no tree — and the derivation
rule moves to the close, where a technical note belongs. It ends with the
three doors the reference ends with, rather than stopping dead.
Every href checked against the built site before committing.

commits.subject: Lerena and Pelaez were one kindred at Trinidad
commits.body:
Item 10 of fifteen: partly advanced, partly blocked, and both said plainly.
WHAT THE DISPENSATION REGISTER GAVE UP WHEN LAID BESIDE TODAY'S OTHER WORK.
Three of its eight Lerena dispensations marry a LERENA to a PELAEZ - Maximo
Pelaez and Maria Lerena at Trinidad in 1885, Juan Lerena and Eduviges Pelaez at
Mercedes in 1894, Vitalino Gregorio Pelaes and Florinda Juana Lerena at Trinidad
in 1909 - and every one of them needed dispensing FOR CONSANGUINITY: twice in
the third degree, once in the second and third accumulated.
The Trinidad baptisms read hours earlier give BERNABE LERENA married to
CASIMIRA PELAEZ, with four children between 1871 and 1885, in that same town.
Neither file says this on its own. The dispensations were searched by surname,
the baptisms by birthplace, and they were written up hours apart. Together they
show that Lerenas and Pelaezes at Trinidad married each other repeatedly across
at least forty years, and that by 1885 the church required a consanguinity
dispensation to let them do it again. They are not two families who met in a
small town; they are one intermarried kindred. A forename crosses too - one of
the six Trinidad Lerena fathers is VITALINO, and the 1909 Pelaez groom is
VITALINO GREGORIO.
Nothing here touches Pablo Armando. There is still no Pablo, no Armando and no
Juan Carlos in the Trinidad set, and the register's own verdict stands: no
Lerena-Lerena dispensation anywhere, 1856-1932. Every Lerena in it marries out.
WHERE IT STOPPED, AND WHY. The actual job was to TURN the register page by page
rather than trust machine handwriting recognition. Not done - the film could
not be located, because FamilySearch's search endpoints went down. Catalogue
search, records search and full-text search all returned "Something Went Wrong"
on repeated attempts from a signed-in session while image tiles kept serving
normally, so it is their outage rather than a block. Three routes to the DGS
were tried and all failed the same way.
The thing that was actually missing before is now in hand: the method is proved.
Navigate /search/film/<DGS>?i=<N>, read the ark from the page title, assemble
the tiles. Only the DGS is wanting, and it is logged as an errand rather than
left looking untouched.

commits.subject: The death registers are three films, and the ark method I published was wrong
commits.body: Item 15 started properly, item 11 carried further, and a correction to a claim I made in a commit message an hour ago. I PUBLISHED A WRONG METHOD, in this file and in a commit message: that a film's image arks cannot be reached by script, so each opening must be got by driving the viewer's next-image control. Wrong, and wrong because I tested one URL form and generalised from it. /ark:/61903/3:1:?i= - ignores i=, keeps the same image. What I tested. /search/film/?i= - RESOLVES TO IMAGE N. What I should have tested. The ark comes out of the page title; it is not in the server-rendered HTML, so fetch() still cannot harvest arks in bulk, but one navigation per image works fine. Also noted: the tile host blocks fetch() cross-origin while serving happily, so the tile grid is found with onload/onerror instead of probing. And the film's i= is NOT the waypoint image number used in the earlier rows - verified against two known openings before relying on it. ITEM 11, with the method fixed: four more openings, acts 921-944, 5-9 August 1882. Avena, Martini, Rodriguez, Acosta, Coppes, Coman, Fernandez, Duarte, Pero, Amaral, Nunez, Cassavola, Ledda, Blasi, Lopez, Lentini, Toledo, Ruiz, Rosas, Flores, Rabellino, Ramosfe, Gallego. No Lerena. That is 780 consecutive baptisms read act by act. ITEM 15: THE ROUTE IS REAL, AND IT IS THREE FILMS, NOT ONE. The catalogue for the parish was read in full - 73 film rows - and the death registers covering the index gap are all filmed: Defunciones 1731-1803 DGS 4531019 Defunciones 1804-1824, 1828-1841 DGS 4531020 Defunciones 1841-1860 DGS 4531021 Defunciones 1861-1864 DGS 4531022 Defunciones 1864-1875 DGS 4531023 This archive had listed only the last. The gaps page asserted that the registers for 1841-1875 "survive and are filmed" - true, but unverified until now and understated by two films. DGS 4531021 was opened: 658 images, unrestricted, and its leader card reads film 1091422, matching the catalogue exactly. AND THE CATALOGUE CONFIRMS THE HARD EDGE: there is no defunciones film after 1875. Deaths 1876-1881 have neither an index section nor a register. That is not a gap this archive can close by working harder, and it is now stated on evidence rather than on inference. Also recovered from the same catalogue and never previously listed here: three Confirmaciones films (the confirmations this archive has long listed as untried - they exist) and two earlier Matrimonios films, 1722-1803 and 1804-1852.

commits.subject: The Rosario Lorenas read at their own schedule: a Peruvian tinsmith
commits.body:
Item 12 of fifteen, closed on the image.
The 1869 census note had asked for exactly this read: "the schedule will show
the household structure - who is head, who is spouse, who is child - and
whether the clerk wrote Lerena, Lorena or Llerena." All six Lorenas turned out
to share ONE image ark, so they are one household on one page, not scattered
through the census as the note supposed.
THE HEAD IS A PERUVIAN TINSMITH FROM LIMA. Agustin Lorena, 40, casado,
"ojalatero" - and his nacionalidad is given as LIMA, with the provincia de su
nacimiento column left BLANK precisely because he is not Argentine. His five
children are Argentine, born in CORDOBA: Guillermo 16 (a tinsmith like his
father), Geronima 15 (confitera, with a trade of her own at fifteen), Mercedes
9, Felix 3, Maria 1. No wife on the schedule though he is recorded married.
AND THE SPELLING IS ANSWERED ON THE PAGE: LORENA - a single L, and the second
letter unmistakably an O.
So they are set down. Guillermo and Geronima were flagged in the register as
the right age to be a parent of a child born in 1882, which is the whole
question - they would have been 29 and 28. But the ONLY reason these six were
of interest was the possibility that "Lorena" was how a Rosario clerk heard
"Lerena", and the schedule says otherwise: a different vowel, a different
country, a different province of origin. Pablo Armando's people were Uruguayan,
and the one Lerena baptised at Rosario before 1879 has parents "naturales del
E. Oriental", read from the act itself.
Recorded as looked at and set down, NOT as an exclusion by arithmetic. Guillermo
could in principle have fathered a child at Rosario in 1882. He is simply no
longer interesting, and now for a reason on an image rather than a hunch.
One echo kept: FamilySearch full text turned up an entire LERENA population at
AREQUIPA, PERU that this archive had never met. A Lorena from Lima belongs with
that population and with nothing in this family.
This also lets the sentence tightened earlier today be tightened the other way:
Bartolome Llerena really is the only credible pre-1882 Rosario candidate - not
because the Lorenas were defined out of the question, but because they were
read and found to be someone else.

commits.subject: Phase 6b: /who — one page per name, because a name is not a person
commits.body:
Four of the seven archives already separated these two ideas. This one did
not, and it is the archive that needed it most.
/people/<person> is one human. /who/<name> is everyone who bore that name,
and the two link to each other. The name page opens by saying how many
people it holds, because the risk it exists to address is a reader assuming
there is only one.
The case that prompted it: twenty different people in this archive are
called Ivan Blazevic. Seven of them carry no dates at all, so the page says
plainly that where two have no dates the archive cannot tell them apart
either. That is a gap, not a tidy answer, and publishing it is the point.
The index lists all 815 names with the 180 held by more than one person
called out, because those are the ones where a reader can go wrong.
A note for whoever touches these next: slugify has to be declared INSIDE
getStaticPaths. Astro lifts that function into its own module scope, where
frontmatter declarations - const or hoisted function alike - are not
visible. It fails at build with "slugify is not defined" and the location
it prints is inside Astro, not your file.

commits.subject: Phase 6a: /trees — every line in the form its evidence supports
commits.body:
Adopts the model the Defranceschi archive worked out. The transferable part
is not the chart, it is refusing to draw a spine you cannot prove, and
saying on the page which of the two a reader is looking at.
Five states, shared across the seven: drawn, web, drawable, route, and
closed — that last for a line followed, tested and shown not to belong.
The state is DERIVED, not asserted. A line is drawn only where this archive
actually publishes a chart of it — checked by looking for a tree component
on the page, not by trusting that a page exists. Everything else is
drawable if there are enough people to chart, a route if there are not.
That check earned itself. Five rows across two archives claimed "drawn"
because a page of that name existed — Barry, Kolbe, Sneyd, Atwell,
Murdoch — and every one of those pages is narrative with no chart on it.
They are demoted, with the gap stated: "No chart of this family has been
drawn — only a page about them."
Two other corrections while building it. Falco's surname pages are
narrative too, so only the Falco line itself is drawn there. And Lerena's
rows are written rather than derived: splitting names on the last word
produced fragments — LERENA), Trinidad), 1911) — which would have shipped
four families that do not exist. Its three rows say what is actually known,
including that Llerena, Larena, Lorena and Lerina are one family spelled
four ways by clerks who had not met the name.

commits.subject: Publish the search index as a file, not just as an import
commits.body:
Caught live, not in a build. These three archives kept searchindex.json in
src/data and imported it, which was fine while each had its own search page
compiled around it. The shared box fetches /searchindex.json at runtime
instead — so on these three the fetch 404'd and search returned nothing,
while the box itself rendered perfectly.
The build now copies the index into public/ before astro runs, so it ships
as a file. The import stays, because the page still counts the rows for its
eyebrow.
Worth recording as the cost of consolidating: the component was right, the
contract was right, the schema validated on all seven — and three sites were
still broken, because nobody had checked that the file the component asks
for is actually served. A schema check is not a request.

commits.subject: Wire in the kit, and one search box for seven archives
commits.body:
Two jobs the roadmap had left open.
THE KIT IS NOW A DEPENDENCY, not a set of copies. Each site installs
@daviddef/archive-kit from GitHub and imports Evidence, SiblingArchives,
Search and archives.json from it; the local duplicates are deleted. The kit
repo had to become public for CI to install it without credentials — it
holds component code and the seven public URLs, all of which is already
published on the sites themselves.
I argued against this earlier on blast-radius grounds and that argument
still stands: a bad publish can now reach all seven at once. What changes
the balance is that the copies had already started to matter — the evidence
ladder, the ring and the search contract are things that have to agree
across archives to mean anything.
SEARCH IS ONE COMPONENT. There were six implementations of the same idea,
91 to 142 lines each, so every improvement had to be made six times or it
silently applied to one site. The box, the ranking and the fold are now
shared; what stays per archive is the index, because only an archive knows
its own data shapes, and the words it uses to describe itself.
That needed one contract. Rows are {k,t,s,h,q} — kind, title, subtitle,
href, and a lowercased accent-folded haystack. Four archives already emitted
exactly that. Booyzen used "x" for the haystack; Falco used {d,k,t,u} with
no folded field at all, and Lerena the same. Their generators now normalise
on the way out, so the fix cannot drift back.
Verified across all seven: 11,778 index rows, zero schema errors, zero bad
hrefs, zero empty haystacks, and every sampled href resolves in the built
site. Driven in a browser on D'Arcy: Saniger 128 results with "Saniger is a
place" first, Hornby 145 with "The Hornby Claim" first, grouped by kind,
and a nothing-found that says it may mean nobody has looked yet.
The search box also gained what none of the six had: aria-describedby on
the input and role="status" aria-live on the count, so a screen reader is
told how many results arrived.

commits.subject: Carry the 1882 register six acts further, and write down why it is slow
commits.body:
Item 11 of fifteen - started honestly rather than claimed.
Opening at image 12, acts 915-920 of 5 August 1882: Francisco Dapple, Justino
Flores, Juan Seguiroma, Inocencio Diez, Miguel Abasto, Juan Agustin Cortes.
No Lerena. That is 756 consecutive baptisms read act by act.
AND A METHOD NOTE THAT COST AN HOUR TO LEARN, recorded so the next person does
not pay for it again. Every image in the film carries its OWN DeepZoom ark, and
the film's list of arks is not reachable by script: the viewer's page state
does not hold it, the ?i=<n> parameter does NOT resolve to a different image,
and the /service/records/waypoint/ endpoints that used to answer now return
404. So the arks already in the table cannot be extrapolated - each one must be
obtained by driving the viewer's next-image control, one image at a time,
before the tiles can be assembled and the margins read.
That is about two round trips per opening on top of the reading. It does not
make the job hard, only slow, which is why it is paused at an exact resume
point - image 13, act 921 - rather than either abandoned or pretended finished.
The priority note already in this file still stands: the POINT of the act-by-act
read was to test whether the 1945 typescript index is complete, and that test is
done and passed across 750 acts. August to December 1882 is completeness, not
discovery.

commits.subject: Check the register against itself, the way the sibling archives do
commits.body:
Items 5, 6 and 13 of fifteen.
ITEM 6 FOUND THE REAL GAP. Comparing this archive against Blazevic, Mazza,
